_comment: Due dates for each week's case study. The quiz gate reads this to decide what is overdue,
which is what lets a green check mean 'everything due so far is done' instead of merely
'nothing detectably wrong'. Times are 11:59pm America/New_York on the date given.
Weeks not listed here are not checked until they have a BRIEF.md. Add weeks 7-15 as their
`brief` holds each week's brief: the audience it is written to and the questions the
student answers. It is the single source for three things - scripts/new_brief.py writes
weeks/weekNN/BRIEF.md from it, the agent reads it to scope the analysis (see CLAUDE.md),
and the week's deck reads it so the slide and the repo cannot drift. Editing a question

week01.title: Entropy in the NFL
questions: How did you define success in short yardage, and why that measure?
Do you see a trend between standardized entropy and your measure of success?
What other information would you want to look at to determine how important entropy is for success?
How would you go about assessing the optimal entropy for a given team?

week02.title: Which kickers can you actually tell apart?
questions: Which kickers, if any, can you separate from league average, and what test did you use to decide?
Brandon Aubrey made 40 of 47 attempts and finished 17th of 31 kickers in FG%. Your GM wants to replace him. How would you advise your GM?
How much does adjusting for the distances a kicker was sent out from change the ranking, and who moves the most?
Does adjusting for distance change your answer about Aubrey? Say why in two sentences.
Create a visual comparing Aubrey to other kickers around the league.
Which kicker do you believe is the best in the league? What other data do you wish you had to answer that question?

week03.title: Is Jorge Polanco's April real?
questions: Before a single at bat in 2025, how likely was it that Polanco would hit .300 this season, and why is that the right starting point?
After April, how much should the manager's view of Polanco move, and why that much rather than more or less?
Of the hitters who started hot, which ones should the manager believe, and what separates them from the rest?
Slide the prior in your visual. Where does the answer stop depending on the prior, and what does that mean for how confident you can be?
Why is the same April average stronger evidence for one hitter than for another?
What else would you want to know before changing the lineup?

week04.title: Why did we lose Super Bowl LX?
week04.audience: Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots
questions: Across the whole game, how closely do EPA and WPA agree, and what does that tell you about what each one is measuring?
On the plays where EPA and WPA disagree most, why do the two models see the same play so differently?
Where in this game do a counting statistic and an efficiency statistic tell two different stories, and which one do you believe?
With two minutes left in a one-score game, which of EPA or WPA should I be looking at, and why?
Which single play would you show the team on film, and what would you say about it?
What is one thing these two statistics cannot tell me about this game?

week05.title: Does running the ball win games, or does winning make you run?
week05.audience: Sean McDermott, head coach of the Buffalo Bills
questions: Your first regression puts a number on what one more rush attempt is worth in final margin. Before you looked at anything else, how much of that number would you have believed, and why?
Once the score a team was playing from enters the model, what happens to the rushing coefficient, and what does that tell you about what the first regression was measuring?
Looking at run share by score state, which way does the arrow run between running the ball and winning? Say how the table supports your answer.
Something is left of the rushing coefficient after the control, and it still clears 0.05. Give two different explanations that would both produce that, and say what data would tell them apart.
An assistant on staff says the analytics say to run more. What would you tell him, in a sentence or two he would accept?
Which of the numbers you produced this week would you put in front of Coach McDermott, and which would you keep on your own screen? Why?
